# Search

Figma: [03m. Search](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-908) · Family: 03 Form & Input · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-26

Four components for finding content across Safqah - a Search Input trigger field, individual Search Result Items, a Search Dropdown organism that combines them, and a Compact Search Trigger for app headers. Used for deal listing search, investor portfolio search, transaction history filters, document/file search, and global app search. The Search Input atom matches the form-family visual conventions but with a search icon (instead of a generic icon) and an optional clear button.

### Search Input

A search field with a leading magnifier and a clear X when it has text. Used above lists to filter or as the top of Search Dropdown.

Level: atom · Part of: Search Dropdown

Use when:
- Filtering a deals list, transactions or investors in place
- The input at the top of Search Dropdown

Don't use when:
- Header or toolbar search with little space: use Compact Search Trigger
- Picking one value from a long list: use Combobox Field
- Non-search text: use Input

Accessibility: Give the field a search role and label, and label the clear button «مسح».

> Not published to the Figma library. Use it by name everywhere; in another Figma file take its published route or copy it from the Syntropy file (syntropy-components, unpublished.md).

### Search Result Item

One result row in Search Dropdown: title only, with subtitle, with icon, or a recent search.

Level: atom · Part of: Search Dropdown

Use when:
- Deal results with meta such as «صكوك · إغلاق نوفمبر 2024»: Type=with-meta
- Document results with a file icon: Type=with-icon
- Recent searches before typing: Type=recent

Don't use when:
- Options of a picker: use Dropdown Item
- Rows in a standalone list screen: use ListItem

Accessibility: Expose rows as options so keyboard highlight (State=selected) is announced.

| Direction | `direction` | variant | ltr, rtl | ltr |

### Search Dropdown

The floating search panel: Search Input on top with results, empty, loading or recent states below. Used for global search and typeahead.

Level: organism · Contains: Search Input, Search Result Item

Use when:
- Global app search across deals, documents and transactions
- Typeahead suggestions while typing
- No matches: State=empty with a recovery hint

Don't use when:
- Filtering the list already on screen: use Search Input alone, no dropdown
- Choosing a form value from options: use Combobox Menu
- Full-page no-results states: use EmptyState

Accessibility: Announce result counts and loading, and debounce queries around 250ms.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| State | `state` | variant | results, empty, loading, recent | results |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | ltr, rtl | ltr |

### Compact Search Trigger

An icon-only search trigger for headers that expands into a full search field (with a keyboard shortcut hint on desktop).

Level: molecule

Use when:
- Search entry in an AppBar or back-office header
- Dense dashboards or table toolbars where a permanent field crowds the layout

Don't use when:
- Search is the main task of the screen: use Search Input
- Quick command access across the app on web: use Command palette

Accessibility: The collapsed icon needs a label like «بحث» and focus must move into the field when it expands.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Search is the primary discovery mechanism across Safqah. Investors search deals by name, sector, or status. Operators search investors by Iqama, phone, or portfolio composition. Compliance officers search documents by deal, date, or upload status. The pattern is the same across all surfaces - type into the Search Input, see results in the Search Dropdown, select a result.

The Compact Search Trigger handles header/toolbar contexts where space is limited - it shows as an icon-only button and expands into the full Search Input on tap. Common in app shells, dashboards, and dense data tables where a permanent search field would crowd the layout.

### At a glance

### Atomic architecture

Four-tier composition: two atoms (Search Input and Search Result Item) + one organism (Search Dropdown) + one alternate trigger (Compact Search Trigger). The dropdown nests the input + multiple result items.

Atom - Search Input · 36 variants

Trigger field with search icon (leading) + value/placeholder + optional clear button (trailing). Variants: 3 sizes × 6 states × 2 directions. The clear button (X) appears only in filled and error states. Visually consistent with the Input organism but tuned for search semantics.

Atom - Search Result Item · 24 variants

Individual result row inside the dropdown. Variants: 4 types (default / with-meta / with-icon / recent) × 3 states (default / hover / selected) × 2 directions. Type=default shows just a title; with-meta adds a subtitle; with-icon adds a leading icon for file/document results; recent adds a "Recent" badge.

Organism - Search Dropdown · 8 variants

Full dropdown panel that combines a Search Input (at the top) with content below. Variants: 4 states (results / empty / loading / recent) × 2 directions. Results state shows section header + 3 result items + "See all results" footer. Empty/loading/recent states are full-panel feedback patterns.

Alternate trigger - Compact Search Trigger · 6 variants

Icon-only button (collapsed) that expands into the full Search Input on tap. Variants: 3 states (collapsed / hover / expanded) × 2 directions. Includes a ⌘K keyboard shortcut hint when expanded. Use in app headers, toolbars, and dense data layouts.

### Patterns - three ways to use Search

Search isn't one thing - it's three distinct patterns with different interaction models. Pick the right pattern for the user's task.

Global app search

Header-level search that finds anything across the app - deals, investors, documents, transactions. Triggered by Compact Search Trigger or ⌘K. Opens the Search Dropdown with categorized results.

Inline filter search

Search within a single list/table to narrow visible rows. No dropdown - typing filters the list in real time. Used on deal listings, transaction tables, investor portfolios.

Typeahead / autocomplete

Search that suggests completions as the user types. Used for tag pickers, currency selectors, country lookups, sector classification. Suggestions in the dropdown become the selected value.

> **Warning:** Don't blur the patterns. Global search should NOT filter the current page - that's confusing. Inline filter search should NOT show a dropdown - typing should immediately filter the table. Typeahead should NOT open a separate page - picking a suggestion should commit the value inline.

### Search Input states

Six states cover the full input lifecycle, identical to the form-family pattern. The clear button appears in filled and error states.

default

Empty resting state. Placeholder "Search" / "بحث", gray search icon, no clear button.

filled

User has typed a query. Value visible in dark text, clear (X) button shown trailing.

hover

Mouse hover (desktop). Subtle border darkening.

focus

Field active. Dark border + 2dp focus ring. Search Dropdown usually opens automatically on focus.

error

Search returned an error or the query is invalid (e.g., regex syntax error). Red border + red text + clear button shown.

disabled

Field is inert. Reduced opacity. Use when search is temporarily unavailable (loading dependencies, no data source).

### Result types

Four Search Result Item types for different content categories. Each type has 3 states (default / hover / selected). The selected state uses bg/brand/primary-subtle for keyboard navigation highlighting.

default

Title only. Use for simple lookup results - investor names, sector tags, currency codes.

with-meta

Title + subtitle. Use for deals (name + sukuk type + closing date), transactions (id + amount + date), documents (name + size + uploader).

with-icon

Title + icon + meta. Use when the result type needs visual identification - file/document results with type icons (PDF, image, contract).

recent

Title + clock icon + "Recent" badge. Use in the empty/initial state to surface the user's last searches without requiring them to retype.

### Dropdown states

Four full-panel states cover every moment in the search lifecycle - initial focus, typing, results, no results.

results

Matching results found. Section header + 3 Search Result Items + "See all results" footer. Most common state during active search.

recent

Initial focus state with no query. Shows the user's recent searches with clock icons + Recent badges. Provides quick access to previous queries.

loading

Query submitted, waiting for results. Centered green spinner + "Searching..." text. Appears for debounced/async searches >150ms.

empty

Query returned zero results. Magnifying glass icon + "No results found" + "Try searching with different keywords". Helps users recover.

### Compact Search Trigger pattern

The Compact Search Trigger handles header/toolbar contexts. Three states match the keyboard shortcut lifecycle: collapsed (icon only) → hover (subtle bg change) → expanded (full input with ⌘K shortcut hint).

collapsed

Icon-only button in the app header. Tap or ⌘K shortcut opens the full search input.

hover

Mouse hover. Subtle bg change indicates the trigger is clickable.

expanded

Full input with shortcut hint. Use this state inline in the header (replaces the collapsed trigger) OR as the opened popup. The ⌘K hint reinforces the keyboard shortcut.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Search components flip layout for Arabic. The Search Input mirrors the search icon to the trailing edge (left in RTL) with the clear button at the leading edge. Result Items right-align text with icons/badges on the opposite side. The Search Dropdown stacks the same way but with mirrored internal alignment.

LTR

English / default. Search icon on the left, value/placeholder left-aligned, clear (X) button on the right. Result Items: leading icon left, text aligned left, optional badge/meta on the right. Apply button label: "Search".

RTL

Arabic. Search icon on the right (leading edge), value/placeholder right-aligned ("بحث"), clear button on the left. Result Items: leading icon right, text right-aligned, optional badge on the left. Search section header: "النتائج" / "البحوث الأخيرة". Empty state: "لا توجد نتائج".

> **Tip:** For Arabic queries, the search backend should handle both Hindi-Arabic numerals (٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩) and Western Arabic numerals (0123456789) interchangeably. A user typing "٢٠٢٤" should match results containing "2024". This is a backend concern but designers should test both formats in mockups.

### Code examples

How to consume Search components in Flutter.

### Flutter - basic Search Input with debounced filter

```dart
// Inline filter search (real-time list filtering)
class _DealListSearchState extends State<DealListSearch> {
  final _controller = TextEditingController();
  Timer? _debounce;
  String _query = '';
  
  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _controller.addListener(() {
      _debounce?.cancel();
      _debounce = Timer(const Duration(milliseconds: 250), () {
        setState(() => _query = _controller.text);
      });
    });
  }
  
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final filtered = widget.deals
      .where((d) => d.name.toLowerCase().contains(_query.toLowerCase()))
      .toList();
    
    return Column(
      children: [
        SafqahSearchInput(
          controller: _controller,
          placeholder: 'Search deals',
          onClear: () => _controller.clear(),
        ),
        const SizedBox(height: 16),
        Expanded(child: DealList(deals: filtered)),
      ],
    );
  }
}
```

### Flutter - typeahead dropdown with async results

```dart
// Typeahead with async fetch + loading/empty states
class _SectorPickerState extends State<SectorPicker> {
  final _controller = TextEditingController();
  Timer? _debounce;
  List<Sector> _results = [];
  bool _loading = false;
  
  Future<void> _onChange(String q) async {
    _debounce?.cancel();
    _debounce = Timer(const Duration(milliseconds: 200), () async {
      if (q.isEmpty) {
        setState(() { _results = []; _loading = false; });
        return;
      }
      setState(() => _loading = true);
      final res = await api.searchSectors(q);
      setState(() { _results = res; _loading = false; });
    });
  }
  
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return SafqahSearchDropdown(
      controller: _controller,
      onChange: _onChange,
      placeholder: 'Search sectors',
      state: _loading
        ? SearchDropdownState.loading
        : _results.isEmpty
          ? SearchDropdownState.empty
          : SearchDropdownState.results,
      results: _results.map((s) => SearchResultItem(
        title: s.name,
        meta: s.tagline,
        onTap: () => widget.onPick(s),
      )).toList(),
    );
  }
}
```

### Flutter - global search with ⌘K shortcut

```dart
// Compact Search Trigger in app header + global ⌘K listener
class AppShell extends StatefulWidget {
  @override
  State<AppShell> createState() => _AppShellState();
}

class _AppShellState extends State<AppShell> {
  bool _searchOpen = false;
  final _shortcuts = <ShortcutActivator, Intent>{
    const SingleActivator(LogicalKeyboardKey.keyK, meta: true): OpenSearchIntent(),
    const SingleActivator(LogicalKeyboardKey.keyK, control: true): OpenSearchIntent(),
  };
  
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Shortcuts(
      shortcuts: _shortcuts,
      child: Actions(
        actions: {
          OpenSearchIntent: CallbackAction(
            onInvoke: (_) => setState(() => _searchOpen = true),
          ),
        },
        child: Scaffold(
          appBar: AppBar(
            actions: [
              SafqahCompactSearchTrigger(
                state: _searchOpen
                  ? CompactSearchState.expanded
                  : CompactSearchState.collapsed,
                onTap: () => setState(() => _searchOpen = true),
                shortcutHint: '⌘K',
              ),
            ],
          ),
          body: _searchOpen
            ? GlobalSearchOverlay(onClose: () => setState(() => _searchOpen = false))
            : widget.body,
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### Flutter - Arabic RTL search

```dart
// Arabic locale - RTL direction + Arabic placeholders + Hindi-Arabic numeral support
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: SafqahSearchInput(
    controller: _controller,
    placeholder: 'بحث',
    onClear: () => _controller.clear(),
    // Normalize Hindi-Arabic numerals to Western Arabic for matching
    normalizeQuery: (q) => q.replaceAllMapped(
      RegExp(r'[٠-٩]'),
      (m) => String.fromCharCode(m.group(0)!.codeUnitAt(0) - 1632 + 48),
    ),
  ),
)
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts.

- **Do** · Debounced inline filtering: Debounce search queries by 200-300ms before filtering or fetching. Reduces network requests and avoids flashing partial results as the user types. The Search Input updates immediately (controlled), but the filter/fetch waits for the typing to pause.
- **Don't** · Debounced inline filtering: Don't filter on every keystroke without debounce - causes noticeable UI lag on larger lists and floods the backend with requests. Don't require Enter to submit either - modern search expects instant feedback once typing stops.
- **Do** · Empty state vs. error: Use the empty state (magnifying glass icon + "No results found" + recovery hint) when the query is valid but returned zero matches. Provide a recovery suggestion: "Try different keywords" or "Check spelling".
- **Don't** · Empty state vs. error: Don't use the error state for "no results" - error means something went wrong (invalid query syntax, backend failure). Don't leave the dropdown blank or hide it entirely on no results - users wonder if the search broke.
- **Do** · Compact vs. full Search Input: Use the Compact Search Trigger in app headers, dashboards, and any layout where space is tight. The icon-only collapsed state preserves header real estate. Pair with a ⌘K shortcut for keyboard users.
- **Don't** · Compact vs. full Search Input: Don't use a full Search Input in a 40dp app header - it dominates the layout. Don't put two search inputs on the same screen (global + inline) without clearly differentiating their scope ("Search app" vs. "Filter this list").
- **Do** · RTL conventions: Use the RTL direction variant for Arabic locales. Search icon moves to the trailing edge (right in RTL = leading edge visually), value/placeholder right-aligned with Arabic text ("صفقات الرياض"). Empty state and section headers in Arabic ("لا توجد نتائج", "البحوث الأخيرة").
- **Don't** · RTL conventions: Don't use LTR direction in Arabic locales. Don't mix Arabic placeholder text with LTR layout - looks broken. Don't leave the dropdown section headers in English in an Arabic UI.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Info:** Three search patterns, one design language - global app search opens a Compact Search Trigger (header), inline filter search uses a standalone Search Input above a list, typeahead opens a Search Dropdown anchored to the input. Don't blur them. The Search Dropdown is reserved for global and typeahead patterns; inline filter should NOT show a dropdown.

> **Warning:** Selected state token: bg/brand/primary-subtle (NOT bg/brand/secondary - that token doesn't exist in the system). This was a locked constraint discovery during the build - silently failed bind when I first tried bg/brand/secondary. Same fallback applies for any "subtle highlight" need across the system.

> **Warning:** Page Dark mode contamination - when the Search page was created it inherited Dark mode from the parent. All semantic backgrounds rendered as #000 (black) instead of resolving to Light. Fix: `searchPage.setExplicitVariableModeForCollection(semantic, "13:0")` to pin the page to Light mode. Same workaround applies to any new page in this file.

> **Warning:** TEXT property defaultValue override pattern hit again (locked constraint #11). When combineAsVariants merges LTR + RTL components, the Value text/Title property defaultValue comes from the first variant. Workaround: removed componentPropertyReferences.characters on per-variant text nodes and set Arabic/state-specific text directly. Means runtime overrides of placeholder/value text work consistently after detach or per-instance.

> **Warning:** Auto-layout sizing collapse hit during the Search Dropdown build - variants showed h:1 after combineAsVariants because primaryAxisSizingMode FIXED clipped vertical content. Fix: set primaryAxisSizingMode=AUTO AFTER combining (not before) and DO NOT call resize() - resize forces FIXED mode. Add to playbook: "set sizing modes without resize on VERTICAL frames that need to hug content".

> **Info:** Clear button visibility: only shown in filled and error states (when there's text to clear). Hidden in default/hover/focus/disabled. This is the standard pattern across Apple, Google, Stripe - clearing is only relevant when there's a value. Don't show the clear X on an empty input.

> **Info:** Search Dropdown elevation: uses drop shadow (offset y:8, blur 24, opacity 0.12) instead of a border. Matches Material 3 / Adobe Spectrum / Linear conventions where dropdowns float above the page. Don't add a border to the dropdown - the shadow alone signals elevation.

> **Info:** ⌘K is a Mac convention. On Windows/Linux use Ctrl+K. On mobile there's no keyboard shortcut - the Compact Search Trigger is tap-only on touch devices. Show the shortcut hint only on desktop. Detect via runtime (kIsWeb && !isMobile) before rendering "⌘K".

> **Info:** Search Result Item types are limited to 4 (default / with-meta / with-icon / recent). If you need a new type (e.g., with-avatar, with-actions), prefer composing INSIDE the with-icon slot by overriding the icon - don't add a new variant axis. The 4 types cover 95% of Safqah search results.

> **Tip:** For Arabic queries, the search backend should normalize Hindi-Arabic numerals (٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩) to Western Arabic numerals (0123456789) before matching. A user typing "صفقة ٢٠٢٤" should match "صفقة 2024" in the database. This is a backend concern but designers should test both formats in mockups - the input doesn't auto-convert.

> **Warning:** FONT WORKAROUND - Same as the rest of the family. All text uses IBM Plex Sans. Font/Size, Font/Line-Height, and Font/Weight all bound to variables on every text node.
